corpus: original model suggestion text with verified acceptance in earlier sessions
finding: No useful primary personal advantage is established. Useful base, pooled and donor advantage is excluded under both interval methods. Uniform advantage is excluded under writer resampling but unresolved under crossed resampling. All primary intervals include zero. Adapted-minus-base donor useful advantage is excluded under writer resampling but remains unresolved under crossed resampling; pooled useful advantage remains unresolved under both methods. Residual uniform useful advantage is excluded under both methods, and all residual intervals include zero. Raw sums retain useful base, pooled and donor uncertainty under both methods, with all model-rival intervals including zero. Raw sums are worse than uniform under both methods. No parity follows.
limits: Additional passes repeat existing text; they do not add personal information. Previously selected model prose reflects suggestion supply and prior choices, not human-authored text or necessarily final retained wording. Sparse histories, transferred calibration-selected rank, shared human units, fixed donor/global training and exposed prompts bound the recipe. No independent human confirmation, human-only language-learning claim, epoch/corpus ranking, population limit, private-goal inference or whole-matrix verdict. Earlier failed/unknown attempts remain separate; no new retry.
